title: FAR Module 5 · TBS 3
html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Contribution Recognition Analysis

Determine which donated services and noncash gifts should be recognized and calculate the related amounts.

Scenario

Community Health Foundation receives the following contributions during the year.

Item 1 — Legal Services

An attorney donates legal services with a fair value of $24,000.

The services require specialized legal skills, and the Foundation otherwise would have hired an attorney.

Item 2 — General Volunteers

Volunteers provide routine clerical assistance valued at $10,000.

The work does not require specialized skills and does not create or enhance a nonfinancial asset.

Item 3 — Donated Equipment

A donor contributes medical equipment with a fair value of $65,000.

There are no donor-imposed restrictions.

Item 4 — Construction Services

Skilled workers donate construction services with a fair value of $30,000 to build an addition to the Foundation's facility.

Required

1. Legal Services Contribution Revenue
2. General Volunteer Services Recognized
3. Donated Equipment Recognized
4. Construction Services Capitalized Into Asset
explanation:
Item 1 — Legal Services

The legal services require specialized skills and otherwise would have been purchased.

Contribution Revenue = $24,000 Related Legal Expense = $24,000

Item 2 — General Volunteers

The routine clerical services do not satisfy the recognition criteria.

Amount Recognized = $0

Item 3 — Donated Equipment

The contributed equipment is generally recognized at fair value.

Equipment = $65,000 Contribution Revenue = $65,000

Item 4 — Construction Services

The donated services create or enhance a nonfinancial asset.

Amount Capitalized = $30,000

CPA Takeaway

  • Specialized donated services may qualify for recognition.
  • Routine volunteer services often are not recognized.
  • Contributed nonfinancial assets are generally measured at fair value.
  • Donated services that create or enhance a nonfinancial asset may be capitalized.
